turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

“I’ve been feeling weaker over the last few months, and I’ve had unintentional weight loss without changing my diet or exercise. I’m also worried about my kidney function because of my family history of kidney disease.”
To better understand your condition, can you tell me more about the nature of your weakness? For example, is it generalized or does it affect specific parts of your body?

“It feels generalized—like my whole body has less stamina—and it doesn’t seem to be limited to one specific muscle group or side. I’ve also noticed the weight loss along with it over the same few months.”
You mentioned unintentional weight loss and generalized weakness. Can you describe your appetite over the past few months? Has it increased, decreased, or remained the same?
“My appetite has decreased somewhat over the past few months, even though I haven’t changed my diet or exercise. It feels like I’m not as hungry as I used to be.”
A decrease in appetite can be associated with various conditions. Have you experienced any other symptoms such as fever, night sweats, or changes in bowel habits?

“I don’t have any fever or night sweats, and I haven’t noticed any changes in my bowel habits. I also haven’t had any rash or other new symptoms—just the generalized weakness, reduced appetite, and the unintentional weight loss.”

The absence of fever, night sweats, and changes in bowel habits helps to narrow down the differential. You mentioned a family history of kidney disease; have you experienced any symptoms related to your kidneys, such as changes in urination, blood in your urine, or flank pain?

“I haven’t noticed any kidney-related symptoms—I’m not having changes in urination, no blood in my urine, and no flank or back pain. It’s mainly just the generalized weakness, decreased appetite, and unintentional weight loss.”

The lack of urinary symptoms or flank pain somewhat reduces the likelihood of an active kidney issue, but your family history is still relevant. Have you noticed any other symptoms such as palpitations, tremors, or heat intolerance that could suggest a metabolic or endocrine disorder?

“I haven’t noticed palpitations, tremors, or heat intolerance—no sweating more than usual or feeling unusually anxious. It’s mostly just the generalized weakness, lower appetite, and unintentional weight loss. I’m mainly concerned about what could be causing it and whether it could be related to my kidneys.”
To further explore the cause of your symptoms, have you experienced any pain or discomfort, particularly in your abdomen or chest, that might give us a clue about the underlying issue?
“I haven’t had any abdominal or chest pain or discomfort. It’s really just the generalized weakness, decreased appetite, and unintentional weight loss.”
